# Day-ahead model (issue 10:00 on D-1): analysis, validation period (generated by `scripts/analyze_dayahead.py`; plan task 9.7)

Design: `docs/experiment_protocol.md`, entry of 2026-10-19. Predictions of `scripts/run_dayahead.py` (validation phase; hyper-parameters and early stopping were chosen on this period, so the numbers are optimistic). 4,367 (day, hour) samples; 181 days with all 24 valid hours. Naive = the better of the two naive baselines on validation (same hour on the latest earlier day). Intervals: 95% paired moving-block bootstrap over whole days (blocks of 28 days, 1,000 resamples, fixed seed).

## Cost of issuing once per day: day-ahead versus the rolling 24 h-ahead forecasts

Same target hours (4,367 hours; 181 complete days in both sets). The rolling forecasts are the 24 h-ahead forecasts of the frozen main run (`h24.npz`), each issued 24 h before its target hour with the latest data at that time; the day-ahead forecasts are issued once at 10:00 on the previous day. The two sets of models use different leads, features and tuning, so this is a descriptive comparison, not a controlled experiment. Difference = day-ahead minus rolling (positive = the fixed issue time costs accuracy).

| model | hourly MAE day-ahead (MW) | hourly MAE rolling 24 h (MW) | difference (95% CI) | energy MAE day-ahead (MU) | energy MAE rolling (MU) | difference (95% CI) | peak MAE day-ahead (MW) | peak MAE rolling (MW) | difference (95% CI) |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---|
| Best naive | 5,536 | 4,931 | +605 (+237 to +890) | 110.9 | 89.6 | +21.2 (+14.3 to +28.3) | 5,348 | 5,131 | +217 (-387 to +827) |
| Ridge | 3,799 | 3,763 | +37 (-435 to +390) | 71.9 | 55.8 | +16.0 (+5.5 to +25.5) | 3,583 | 3,480 | +103 (-447 to +453) |
| XGBoost S4 | 3,585 | 3,170 | +415 (+245 to +575) | 69.2 | 54.3 | +14.9 (+10.8 to +19.3) | 3,526 | 3,211 | +314 (-207 to +867) |
| LSTM L4 | 3,867 | 3,273 | +595 (+423 to +775) | 74.0 | 54.6 | +19.4 (+14.8 to +24.3) | 3,658 | 3,082 | +576 (+176 to +1,027) |

Differences whose interval includes zero are not distinguishable.

## Caveats

- 181 complete days from one validation half-year. Intervals reflect day-to-day sampling noise inside that period, not year-to-year variation.
- Scenario A: no forecast weather, so the day-ahead problem is harder than in practice where weather forecasts exist; forecast temperature helped at 24-72 h in the main study.
- The origin is the demand value of the hour starting at 10:00; the issue time and the availability of that value are assumptions of the design.
- XGBoost and the LSTM are pooled over the 24 target hours (one model each), ridge has one model per target hour; the per-hour XGBoost and a 24-output LSTM were not run.
- The test year has been used several times for declared analyses; this is a further use, with the design fixed beforehand.
